prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Stronger economy, fairer society: opportunity for everyone

Core approach
- Finish the job of repairing the public finances fairly by 2017/18: mix spending restraint with taxes on the wealthiest, banks, big business and polluters; no rises in headline Income Tax, NI, VAT or Corporation Tax. New fiscal rules: debt falls each year (outside recessions) and the current budget balances over the cycle, while allowing borrowing for productive investment.
- Cut taxes on work by raising the Personal Allowance to £12,500; clamp down on avoidance/evasion, restrict non‑dom status and introduce a High Value Property Levy on £2m+ homes.

Prosperity that lasts
- Build a high‑skill, low‑carbon, innovative economy: double economy‑wide innovation spend; expand the Green Investment Bank; legally bind power‑sector decarbonisation to 50–100g CO2/kWh by 2030; end unabated coal by 2025; back renewables, storage, CCS and community energy.
- Modern infrastructure: HS2 as part of a national high‑speed network, major rail electrification, East‑West Rail, Transport for the North, resilient links to the South West; low‑emission transport and clean air zones.
- Open, trading Britain in a reformed EU: complete the Single Market (digital, energy, services), support fair trade deals, welcome high‑skill migrants and overseas students, complete universal high‑speed broadband.

Real help for families
- Childcare: towards 20 hours free for all 2–4s and from 9 months for working parents; complete Tax‑Free Childcare; include 85% childcare support in Universal Credit.
- Work that pays: Living Wage in central government; stronger enforcement of the minimum wage; tackle zero‑hours abuse; transparency on gender pay.
- Fair welfare: time‑limited 1% uprating cap to balance the books (exempt disability/parental benefits); sensible housing reforms; protect young people’s safety net.
- Pensions: make the triple lock permanent; continue auto‑enrolment; fair, simpler tax relief review.

Opportunity through education
- Protect funding from nursery to 19 and maintain/enhance the Pupil Premium; end child illiteracy and innumeracy by 2025.
- Qualified teachers in every class; independent standards authority; a slim core curriculum including PSHE, financial literacy and age‑appropriate SRE.
- Double the number of businesses hiring apprentices; fair access and transparency in universities; discount bus travel for 16–21s.

Health and care with mental health at its heart
- Invest the extra £8bn a year the NHS in England needs by 2020; equal status for mental and physical health with new waiting‑time standards and £500m more a year by 2016/17.
- Join up health and social care with pooled local budgets by 2018; better GP access; support carers with a £250 annual bonus; implement the Dilnot cap; raise care quality and staff standards.

Homes, warmth and security
- Build 300,000 homes a year, including Garden Cities; a Housing Investment Bank and direct commissioning; more affordable homes; Rent to Own and Help to Rent; stronger tenant rights.
- A Green Buildings Act: cut bills and emissions; long‑term goal of Band C for all homes (fuel‑poor and rentals by 2027); council tax discounts for major efficiency upgrades.

Green Britain Guarantee
- Five Green Laws on nature, zero‑waste, green transport, zero‑carbon by 2050, and green buildings; plant a tree for every child; new National Nature Parks; clean air by 2020.

Freedom, fairness and safer communities
- Protect the Human Rights Act; a Digital Bill of Rights; a second Freedoms Act; oppose blanket surveillance.
- Tackle discrimination (LGBT+, women, BAME, disability); teach consent; end FGM and domestic abuse.
- Prevent crime, put victims first, and cut reoffending with rehabilitation and smarter sentencing; evidence‑based drug policy focused on health.

Power to people and places
- Home Rule within a federal UK; Constitutional Convention; STV for elections and votes at 16; cap big money in politics; devolution on demand in England.

Britain in the world
- Lead in a reformed EU; uphold international law; meet 0.7% aid; secure a global climate deal; modern defence via a Single Security Budget; step down the nuclear posture while maintaining deterrence.
